dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: The main predicate, defined as exactly the conjunction displayed on the right side of the target equivalence.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The theorem is the definitional unfolding of this Riemann-interface-flux predicate.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: A data record for an m-component interface-flux update, parameterized by a solver-information type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It stores cell averages, origin values, a solver method, a positive scale candidate, and updated cell averages.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection selecting cell averages indexed by integer cell and component in Fin m.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: These states provide the left and right data at every interface and the old value in the update formula.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection selecting the real flux scale.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It must be positive and multiplies the difference of adjacent interface fluxes.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection selecting the Riemann-solver method record.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its mode, solver, information-to-flux map, and two validation predicates appear throughout the target.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection selecting updated cell averages indexed by integer cell and component.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target equates these values with the stated conservative flux-difference update.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection selecting a component vector at each integer interface to use as the value at x=0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It completes the piecewise local Riemann datum, while the left/right Riemann predicate itself leaves the origin unconstrained.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection from a solver method selecting the map from solver information to a flux vector.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It turns the information returned for neighboring states into the interface flux used by the update.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection selecting an opaque predicate that a flux vector is a physical-flux approximation for a left/right state pair.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The flux produced at every interface must satisfy this predicate.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection selecting an opaque predicate that solver information is suitable for a mode and a left/right state pair.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The information returned by solve at every interface must satisfy this predicate.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection selecting the solver map from a pair of states to Information.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is applied to the adjacent cell-average states at every interface.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection selecting the solver-mode value.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is required to equal one of the two constructors and is passed to the suitability predicate.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef016

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef017

binders: m is an arbitrary natural number, so states and fluxes are vectors Fin m → Real.
Information is an arbitrary type of Riemann-solver information.
data is an interface-flux data record containing integer-indexed cell averages, integer-indexed origin values, an abstract solver method, a real flux scale, and integer-indexed updated cell averages.
conclusions: LocalDef001 data holds if and only if the flux scale is positive; the solver mode is one of its two constructors; every integer interface i has the prescribed local piecewise Riemann datum with left state U_{i−1} and right state U_i; the solver output for that pair is declared suitable; its information-derived flux is declared a physical-flux approximation; and every updated cell average equals U_i − fluxScale·(F_{i+1}−F_i), where F_j is obtained by solving the pair (U_{j−1},U_j) and converting the returned information to a flux.
mathematical_definitions: At interface i, the local datum q_i(x) is U_{i−1} for x<0, data.valueAtOrigin i for x=0, and U_i for x>0.
The left/right Riemann-data predicate checks only q_i(x)=U_{i−1} for x<0 and q_i(x)=U_i for x>0.
For any interface j, F_j = fluxFromInformation (solve U_{j−1} U_j).
The componentwise finite-volume update is updatedCellAverages i = U_i − fluxScale • (F_{i+1} − F_i).
translation.proposition_plain_english: The named interface-flux predicate is exactly the checklist for an abstract two-state Riemann-solver update: use adjacent cell averages as the one-sided local data, require the solver information and resulting flux to satisfy stored validation predicates, and update each cell by a positive-scale difference of its right and left numerical interface fluxes.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The equivalence only unfolds LocalDef001 and therefore proves no independent analytic or numerical property.
Suitability of solver information and physicality of the flux are arbitrary predicate fields.
Only positivity of fluxScale is required; no CFL upper bound or relationship to a time step, mesh width, or wave speed is encoded.
The two solver-mode constructors have no recoverable semantic labels in the blind dossier.
The component count m may be zero, in which case all Fin m component assertions are vacuous and states are empty functions.
The Riemann-data condition imposes no value at x=0; the stored origin value is therefore mathematically irrelevant to that condition.
No consistency identity F(U,U)=f(U), conservation theorem, stability, accuracy, entropy condition, or convergence claim is stated.
ambiguities: The intended algorithms represented by the two solver modes are not identifiable from their anonymized constructors.
The meanings of the suitability and physical-flux-approximation predicates are opaque.
The physical interpretation of fluxScale is not specified by the proposition.
